title: Beeswax birthday candles
subtitle: Hand-dipped taper candles for celebration cakes
excerpt: Small hand-dipped taper candles made by repeatedly dipping a cotton wick in melted beeswax to build up layers. Beeswax burns cleanly, drips less than paraffin, and carries a gentle honey scent without added fragrance. A batch of twelve candles uses about 100 g of beeswax and burns for fifteen to twenty minutes each.
sourceNotes: Hand-dipping beeswax candles: Candlemaking by Betty Oppenheimer (1999, Storey Publishing). Beeswax melt point: approximately 62 to 64°C (USDA AMS Beeswax Standards 2019). Burn time estimate: 1 cm of 10 mm diameter beeswax taper = approximately 20 to 25 minutes at a still-air burn. Pre-waxing the wick before dipping reduces wick curl.

recipe.yieldDescription: 12 birthday candles (~10 cm tall, 8 to 10 mm diameter)
recipe.batchNotes: A deeper pot makes dipping easier. Work with as much wax as the dipping vessel allows; keep beeswax between 70 to 75°C throughout.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Beeswax birthday candles keep indefinitely in a cool, dry cupboard. Make a season ahead of time, they are stable for years.
recipe.temperatureNote: Keep the beeswax at 70 to 75°C throughout the dipping session. Below 68°C the wax solidifies on contact before each layer bonds properly; above 78°C the new layer melts the previous one off.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Effectively indefinite if kept cool and dry. Beeswax does not go rancid. A white surface bloom (bloom) on the wax is normal and can be polished off with a warm cloth.

glossaryTerms.definition: A white, powdery or greasy surface haze that forms on beeswax candles after cooling. It is caused by temperature fluctuation during cooling or storage and does not affect the burn. Polish with a warm cloth or ignore it.

content.text: Beeswax birthday candles are small hand-dipped tapers made by repeatedly dipping a cotton wick in melted beeswax to build up thin layers until the candle reaches the right diameter. Beeswax burns cleanly, drips less than paraffin, and carries a gentle honey scent without added fragrance. A batch of twelve uses about 100 g of beeswax; each candle burns for fifteen to twenty minutes.

items.prepNote: yellow or white beeswax pellets; melt in a narrow deep pot that accommodates a 10 cm candle
natural cotton wick, 15 cm lengths (cut from bulk wick); size 2/0 or 3/0 is suitable for birthday-candle diameter

content.text: Cut twelve 15 cm lengths of cotton wick. Dip each length once in the melted wax and pull it out straight, holding it taut for a few seconds until the wax sets. This first coat stiffens the wick so it hangs straight during subsequent dips.

Melt the beeswax in a narrow, deep pot over a water bath. Keep the wax at 70 to 75°C throughout. Use a thermometer: below 68°C the wax sets before each new layer bonds; above 78°C the layers melt off.

Dip a wick into the wax for two seconds, then pull it out in a slow, steady movement. Hold it vertical and straight for five seconds while the layer sets. Dip the next wick while the first one cools. Work through the set of twelve in rotation so each candle has time to cool between coats. Repeat until the candles reach 8 to 10 mm in diameter, typically 20 to 25 dips.
Cut the base of each candle flat with a sharp knife so it fits a standard birthday-candle holder. Trim the top wick to 6 mm. Leave to cool fully before storing.
Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Beeswax candles keep for years. A white surface
may develop on the wax surface over time, polish off with a warm cloth or leave it. It does not affect the burn.
